speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Public agencies have been working closely with SG Enable to drive the hiring of persons with special needs in the Public Service.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Our efforts include advertising suitable vacancies on SG Enable's job portal and participating in career fairs and programmes, such as job shadowing, internship and mentorship organised by SG Enable.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Agencies can also tap on SG Enable’s Workplace Disability Inclusive Index, advisory and consultancy services, attend disability management workshops and training, or access SG Enable's online resources.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Once these individuals are in our employment, public agencies also work with SG Enable to train and integrate them into the organisations through employee training, workplace modifications and job redesign.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: For instance, the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth had installed magnifier software and equipment to help two officers with special needs read documents on the computer screen and in hard copies more clearly and easily.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The Ministry of Manpower (MOM) had also modified its workplace to improve wheelchair accessibility for an officer with limited physical mobility and provided a modified telephone and headset to enable her to make and receive phone calls with greater ease.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Beyond tapping on the support schemes provided by SG Enable, the Public Service is also committed to providing opportunities for our officers with special needs to develop their skills and enhance their ability to perform work in different areas.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: One good example is Vital, which employs a number of persons with special needs in the Payroll and Claims division.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Initially, these officers were assigned duties in claims verification.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Once they were familiar with claims verification, they were exposed to payroll processing and eventually were able to take on work in this area as well.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Our officers with special needs are also given a fair chance to be considered for promotion, if they demonstrate good performance and the ability to take on a larger role.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: We hope that our commitment to supporting the employment of differently-abled individuals, and the positive experience that we have had doing so, will encourage other employers to come on board in this effort.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: To this end, some of our public agencies like MOM and the Government Technology Agency (GovTech) have worked with SG Enable to feature some of our officers with special needs in their outreach efforts.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Speaker, I thank the Minister for the clarification.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: I am very heartened to hear that we have 300 differently-abled persons within the Public Service.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Can the Minister share a little bit about some of the challenges that the Public Service may face in having more of such differently-abled persons to join the service?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Because I understand that the Service is 170,000 strong and 300 is an amazing effort.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: But I am wondering if there are challenges that are preventing the Service from bringing in more.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: The other question is whether the Minister could share some of the successes.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: So, success stories of working with the differently-abled within the Service, so that the other employers can also take heed.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, we look at the abilities rather than the disabilities.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I know he is also very supportive of this community.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I want to take this opportunity to honour the good Public Service agencies that are very progressive and very inclusive, like the National Library Board (NLB), Vital, Ministry of Health (MOH) Holdings and so forth.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I ask the Minister and the Public Service to share some of these success stories as my fellow colleague, Ms Anthea Ong, has mentioned.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I want to ask if the Minister would consider putting in a more ambitious target.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: What we are seeing is only 300 out of more than 100,000 employees who are persons with special needs.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I know the Government is generally quite allergic to quotas in this aspect, but I am hoping that at least the Public Service can set an example, a model.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Perhaps install some targets, for example, 1% to 2% as a start, so that the rest of us in the country can look towards learning from what is possible.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I feel strongly that when the Government puts its heart to something, it always gets done and done fairly well.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: So, I hope the Minister will consider my suggestion for at least a target in the Public Service to hire persons with special needs, including those with mental health.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This is something that is close to my heart and I have discussed this long and hard with my staff as to whether we should set a target.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Today, we do not set a target, but we have something better than that.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: If we set a target, people usually try to meet the target.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But I really do not want people to meet the target for the sake of meeting the target.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I want people to look at the people based on what they can do, to focus on their abilities rather than their disabilities and fit them into the job, redesign the job to fit the person.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The best incentive for the Public Service to do this in a manpower crunch situation is this: we have a separate quota.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In a sense, we do not count in against the usual manpower headcount.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, you can employ more people that is not under your headcount.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And every agency has great incentive to do this when there is a manpower tightness in the labour market.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: I am really heartened by Minister's sharing of that particular hiring scheme.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I think I did not use that word but Ms Denise Phua used the word.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We want people to really focus on the abilities of what this community can provide.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Today, as for the Public Service, it is not a secret as in nobody knows about it.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But I think what we can encourage people to do is to see the examples of those who have embraced the community with special needs and how they have played a constructive and positive part in this whole journey.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And that will encourage more people to come on board.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Today, I looked at the numbers, they are not under any constraints.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This is over and above what the usual manpower quotas will be.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, I think there is great scope for us to do more and I will take the Member's suggestion that we can definitely do more to promote good practices and share some of the best practices in many of these jobs available.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Personally, I have visited some of the call centres, including the private ones, where people think that people with special needs are less efficient.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Because sometimes when we have a disability in one of our faculties, we become much more focused in another, and they end up being even more productive than what we call normal people.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, there are some stories that we can share to encourage our people to embrace them.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: At the same time, we all need to take some effort to redesign some of the jobs in our respective organisations.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, my assurance to the public is that, for the Public Service at least, they have the latitude to go forth in this, and they are not constrained by the manpower quotas in the usual sense.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Ms Denise Phua, I will permit this only if it is different from the points you have made earlier.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: I think we are sharing from the same side.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: So, I do not think it is an argument but really how far do we go.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: I think besides the good scheme that you have mentioned just now, I wonder if you could also install a recognition programme —

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: When I was in some countries, in the public school system, for example, inclusive schools, were actually recognised.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: The schools who got awarded felt like they really made a difference, and I do not know if that feature or culture can be installed in the Public Service as well.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: It is not just having an extra headcount, it is doing something really right and doing it well and that they can be recognised and be seen as models.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: Organisations like NLB, MOH Holdings, Vital and so forth, they are really doing a good job, and I think we should uphold them, raise them, let them be recognised, and others in the rest of the sectors can learn from them.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: I wonder if that could also be a reason why that information is not known and whether the Public Service is also looking to prohibit that practice if it is actually still going on.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: Can I also take this opportunity to formally apologise for being late to the Speaker and also to Senior Parliamentary Secretary Faishal.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Many of the declarations on medical things are in confidence, so when we ask people to let the organisation know, it is not with the view of a punitive action.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It is, in fact, to make sure that there are some special needs that the organisation should be aware of, then to make sure that we can better take care of the person.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Let us say the person, for whatever personal reason, decides not to declare medical in staff confidence questions, I think we can understand that.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But I also want to reassure the House that it is not for punishment or to blacklist anybody.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In fact, if anybody declares a medical condition, it is so that we can better take care of the person and that we will not unnecessarily stress the person beyond the point of their capability.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Just to follow on Ms Denise Phua's point, I agree with the Member that we can do more to help our people be aware of the opportunities and the potential of the special needs community.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: I think the greatest rewards for our public servants who embrace such things is because they know deep in their hearts that they are doing the right thing.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: They are upholding the kind of values that we exemplify and this is much more important to them than any tangible, physical awards.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: That should be how we go forward as a society.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It is the kind of values that we want to express, rather than tangible rewards per se.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: The concern that people may have when filling in these forms to declare their health conditions to their supervisors is that they are concerned they may be perceived as perhaps not up to the task if they declare a pre-existing or past mental condition.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Therefore, that may affect their promotion opportunities and advancement opportunities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: So, what can the Public Service do to assure individuals that this should not be a concern, that they should declare everything so that they can be appropriately managed and that they will not be at any risk of not advancing as far in their careers as other people?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In fact, we want the person to be safe, we want the workplace that they work in to be safe, so we need to understand their medical conditions and we see how we can help them in that sense.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: That assurance comes from me down to every level in the Public Service.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The safety of the individual, the safety of the team and the crew are of utmost concern to us when they conduct any jobs.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We always teach our people, even from my own organisation – I grew up in the SAF – that we must make sure that we know ourselves, know the capabilities of ourselves, know the capabilities of our team members so that we do not put one another in danger, so that we can all accomplish the mission together.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: That philosophy remains that we should not see their declaration of medical condition as a blacklisting exercise or in any way impeding their progress.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It is an exercise to make sure that we know the capabilities of the respective members, the limitations of the respective members, so that we can put everyone's potential to good use.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: The Minister is usually very analytical, perceptive and strategic.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The job fit requires us to understand the capabilities of the individuals concerned.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The job fit also requires the organisations to have a clear understanding of what the individual is capable of.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: From my experience in the Ministry of Social and Family Development, it is not just in the Public Service sector alone.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Many organisations can do much better than in our efforts to try to understand the capabilities, the abilities of the people that we are talking about and not the disabilities of the people we are talking about.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: That requires a bit of effort and that is another area that we can do much more together, with SG Enable's help, to see how we can redesign the job processes.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Sometimes, it is not as difficult as we imagine it to be.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, these are the two key factors as to why it is so.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And this is something that we can all help, together with SG Enable.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: These are my own experiences of how we can lift the numbers of people with special needs in employment.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: However, in the job market, generally, that is being seen as discriminating to a large extent.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: It is both coming from a stigma that is in society as well, to self-stigma of the individual.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: Would Minister Chan be open to considering not having a practice as such but, once a candidate or applicant is employed, to then have the human resource (HR) team work with the person to give him or her support once he or she comes forward to declare their conditions?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It would be quite bad for us to put someone into a job that demands something from that person which is beyond what that person is capable of doing.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We should be very careful to do that for the safety of the individual and the safety of the organisation.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And that is my assurance to the House.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Clerk will now proceed to read the Order of the Day.
